## Natural history notes

A native aromatic perennial shrub in the mint family, characterized by stiff narrow leaves and dense clusters of lavender to purple flowers. Florida Pennyroyal occurs primarily in dry, sandy habitats such as scrub, sandhill, pine flatwoods, and open disturbed uplands, where it thrives in full sun and well-drained soils. Crushing the foliage releases a strong mint-like fragrance, and the showy flowers attract bees, butterflies, and other pollinators. The species is especially characteristic of peninsular Florida and is well adapted to drought and the open conditions maintained by periodic fire.
